reason: The text demonstrates limited instances of ingratitude. Most notably, Israelite officers (שֹֽׁטְרֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל) encounter Moses and Aaron and say 'May Yahweh look upon you and judge, for you have made us stink in the sight of Pharaoh and his servants,' blaming their leaders for their hardship. Additionally, Moses himself expresses doubt toward Yahweh, questioning 'Why have you done evil to this people? Why did you send me? Since I came to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has treated this people badly, and you have not saved your people at all.' However, these instances are isolated moments, and much of the text shows the Hebrews obediently following their leaders' instructions and maintaining faith in God's eventual deliverance.
